text:
- **chief complaint:** routine follow-up of chronic conditions (depression, asthma, diabetes).
- **history of present illness:** the patient is managing depression but had self-tapered Prozac and has periodic depressive episodes. Asthma flared during a bad pollen season and with heat, and the patient uses the inhaler when temperatures exceed about 85°F. Diabetes control slipped after a weekend of poor diet while traveling. The patient reports lightheadedness and dizziness with heat and exertion, and exercises by biking about 45 minutes most mornings.
- **physical examination:** no acute distress; no cervical lymphadenopathy; thyroid not enlarged; faint bilateral expiratory wheezing; regular heart rate and rhythm; soft abdomen; no lower extremity edema. PFTs look good, chest x-ray shows no pneumonia, and hemoglobin A1c is elevated.
- **symptoms experienced by the patient:** dizziness, lightheadedness, shortness of breath, knee pain, wheezing, depressive episodes.
- **new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages:** metformin increased to 1,000 mg twice daily; Symbicort 2 puffs twice daily during summer months; Zoloft 25 mg once daily (replacing Prozac 20 mg daily); albuterol 2 puffs every 4–6 hours as needed (continued).
- **follow-up instructions:** repeat hemoglobin A1c in 3 months; monitor blood sugar at home; the patient will see how well Zoloft is tolerated; nurse to assist with the new regimen.
